neighbours.label: ' subject' / ' scope' as the aboutness noun in 'the subject of …' and 'within/outside the scope of …' (weaker on 'the topic/focus of'; not a school subject, a test subject or a rifle scope)
fire: The collapse of the fishery has long been the subject of bitter argument.
Tax policy is beyond the scope of this report.
His wartime letters are the subject of a forthcoming book.
Hardware faults fall outside the scope of this guide.
The origin of the manuscript remains the subject of much speculation.
Such details lie within the scope of the second chapter.
The final years of the painter were the subject of a recent documentary.
Legal advice is outside the scope of our service.
quiet: The collapse of the fishery has long been the cause of bitter hardship.
Tax policy is explained in the last part of this report.
His best subject in college was chemistry.
The hunter fitted a new scope to his rifle.
The origin of the manuscript remains unknown to scholars.
Each test subject was given a short questionnaire.
The final years of the painter were spent in a small coastal village.
The email had no subject line and no greeting.

notes: Probes: 'the subject of heated debate' 0.76, 'beyond the scope of this essay' 0.70, 'the subject of a new biography' 0.68; 'the topic of' 0.49, 'subject to availability' 0.47, 'the focus of' 0.38, 'theme of' 0.21, 'the cause of' 0.15; 'favourite subject at school' 0.05, 'rifle scope' 0.05. The declared token trigger over-counts: the tokens fire only in the aboutness sense.
